images.title: How many pieces fit?
images.purpose: Recap predicting the size of a quotient in a real problem: a 2.4 m ribbon cut into 0.3 m pieces gives 8 pieces, more than 2.4.
images.composition: One long ribbon across the centre split into equal pieces, with a total bracket above and one equation line below; generous white space.
exact_structure: One long horizontal ribbon strip, a grey #6B7280 bracket above the whole strip labelled 2.4 m.
The ribbon is divided by thin dark lines into exactly 8 equal pieces, alternating teal #0072B2 and amber #E69F00, starting with teal.
Under the first piece only: a small bracket labelled 0.3 m.
Below the ribbon: one line 2.4 ÷ 0.3 = 24 ÷ 3 = 8, with 8 in green #009E73.
Bottom right: a reddish purple #CC79A7 tag reading divisor less than 1, so quotient bigger than 2.4.
labels: divisor less than 1, so quotient bigger than 2.4
rejection: any value other than 8 as the answer
images.takeaway: Predict first: a divisor less than 1 gives a quotient bigger than the dividend, so 2.4 ÷ 0.3 = 8.
images.description: A 2.4 m ribbon split into 8 equal pieces of 0.3 m, with 2.4 ÷ 0.3 = 24 ÷ 3 = 8.
images.context: Shown beside the practice task on dividing decimals in everyday problems.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to count the pieces and check that 8 × 0.3 = 2.4.

image_decisions.why: A fresh everyday picture recaps predicting quotient size without using any practice question's numbers.
